summary: Busy tape. The Fed held at 3.75%-4.00% with two dissents for a hike (Polymarket 82% on a December hike, 10-year near 5%), Alphabet is down about 11% premarket on a Q3 miss, and DoorDash confirmed the $65/share Instacart deal, so CART is now a long-dated merger-arb name. Today's earnings wave (INCY, BDC, HWM, LNG) is resolved from filings, but AAPL (10-29 file estimate vs a Benzinga-cited 11-02), BJRI, CVS and CALX are still unverified, and a block of names reports 11-02 to 11-05 (CLX with a CEO change, IDXX held, TPR, SMG, DBX). Per L2 every symbol in the input is covered below; per the graded record (news-analyst 10 right / 15 wrong, mostly stale file dates), dates are checked against filings first.

event_risk.why: No 8-K 2.02 or results headline yet. The file estimate is 10-29 (today) but Benzinga pieces on 10-27 and 10-28 cite Nov 2 ('earnings due next week'), so Nov 2 looks likelier; either is inside the 5-day window. Date is approximate and unverified. Fresh read: reports that Apple told suppliers to raise iPhone Duo output on strong demand (positive), against the hinge-crack replacement program flagged 10-27. Korea fine, Musk jab and the STMicro/Bezos/O'Leary AAPL-tagged pieces are noise.
Estimated earnings today (approximate). No filing and no results headline in the input, so unverified; likely after the close. Last item remains Citi's PT cut to $70 (Neutral) from 10-23.

Resolved into a deal: DoorDash confirmed it will buy Instacart at $65.00/share (about $17B, at least 75% cash, close expected by 2028); 8-K 1.01/8.01 filed today, trading halted and resumed premarket. Q3 also reported (8-K 2.02; adj EPS $0.60 vs $0.63 est, sales $1.095B vs $1.071B), so the 11-09 estimate is moot. Continues the 10-23 to 10-28 takeover thread. Upside is now capped near the offer, with a long, regulatory-exposed timeline (FTC personalized-pricing information request to Instacart on 10-28, noted in the same thread). Any buy is merger-arb, not an operating thesis.

Adds to the negative preview drift (JPMorgan Underweight/$83, UBS on pressured organic sales).

Law-firm notices are solicitations, but a surviving class action is a real overhang. Follows DA Davidson's PT cut to $382 (10-26).

Alphabet is set for its worst day since March 2020 (about -11% premarket, Q3 miss on search slowdown despite cloud strength), a possible second-largest one-day value loss on record. Amazon and other mega-caps report this week; the AI-bubble/capex thread (Burry, CoreWeave slump, Bessent dismissing neocloud debt fears) continues from 10-20. Fed hawkish hold adds multiple pressure.

Back near $80k after the Fed; Cowen says a hot PCE could push yields up and trigger a Q4 selloff (September PCE came in at 3.6%, as expected; Q3 GDP 3.4% beat). Polymarket puts a December hike at 82%. Strategy was due to report 10-29 per earlier notes (not in today's input, unverified). Constructive but non-binding: Hagerty says Strategic Bitcoin Reserve could expand after the CLARITY Act, Google is preparing a crypto custody platform. No exchange failure or adverse regulation. Calacanis/Cardone, Scaramucci and Polymarket politics items are opinion.

notable.headline: DoorDash confirms Instacart acquisition at $65.00/share (~$17B, at least 75% cash, close by 2028); Instacart Q3 EPS $0.60 vs $0.63, sales $1.095B vs $1.071B
notable.read: Resolves the 10-23 to 10-28 takeover thread into a signed deal (8-K 1.01). The stock now trades as merger-arb: upside capped near $65, a long timeline with regulatory exposure (FTC pricing information request, 10-28), and the earnings print no longer matters.

notable.headline: Alphabet stock set for worst day since March 2020 on Q3 miss; Fed holds at 3.75%-4% with two dissents for a hike, Polymarket 82% on a December hike
notable.read: Confirms the AI-capex worry flagged since 10-20 with a hard fact: search slowdown overshadowing cloud. Paired with a hawkish hold, 10-year yield near 5% and 3.6% PCE, the setup for tech and rate-sensitive ETFs is worse than yesterday.

notable.headline: Fed holds, two officials push for a hike; Warsh plans fewer rate votes (six by 2028); 10-year near 5%
notable.read: Duration risk is two-way only in name; the data (PCE 3.6%, GDP 3.4%) and December hike odds skew toward higher yields. Affects TLT most, IEF and BND less.

notable.headline: Clorox appoints Fabian Garcia as CEO effective Jan 5, 2027, succeeding Linda Rendle (8-K 5.02)
notable.read: A planned handover announced days before the roughly 11-02 print, on top of two negative preview notes. Adds uncertainty about guidance tone rather than a broken thesis; the print is the real risk.

notable.headline: Wells Fargo maintains Overweight on Tapestry, lowers PT to $150
notable.read: Fourth PT cut in about a week (UBS, Jefferies, Baird, now Wells Fargo) ahead of the 11-05 print; every firm keeps its rating. Continues the 10-21 drift flag, which has not come to nothing.

notable.headline: Belden Q3: revenue $965.9M beat, net loss $11.4M, Q4 GAAP EPS guide $0.24-$0.39 vs $1.73 est; $100M data-center fiber deal
notable.read: Headline revenue and adjusted numbers are fine, but the GAAP guide implies a large charge and the stock is lower premarket. Resolves the 10-27/28 earnings flag.

notable.headline: Howmet raises FY26 EPS guide to $5.49-$5.51 vs $5.33 est; Q4 guide above consensus; bigger buyback
notable.read: Clean beat and raise, the best print of the day's earnings wave. Resolves the earnings flag.

notable.headline: Cheniere Q3 EPS $5.65 vs $4.22; dividend raised to $0.625
notable.read: Large beat plus a 12.6% dividend increase; resolves the 10-27/28 flag. Oil and Iran swings remain the macro risk.

notable.headline: Incyte Q3 sales $1.557B vs $1.470B est; FY26 sales guide raised to $5.21B-$5.30B
notable.read: Resolves the stale 10-27 estimate and the open L2 item. Benzinga's 'vs $5.929B est' on the guide is inconsistent with the quarter and should not be trusted as a miss.

notable.headline: Johnson Fistel investigating derivative claims against Domino's after denial of motion to dismiss in securities class action
notable.read: Held name. A securities class action over international-growth disclosures has survived a motion to dismiss; law-firm notices are marketing, but this is a real legal overhang on top of the 10-26 PT cut.

notable.headline: FTC orders Walmart, Target, Uber, DoorDash, Instacart and others to disclose pricing and wage-setting data practices
notable.read: A sector-wide information request, not an action against Walmart. Fits the shelf-label and dynamic-pricing scrutiny already noted for KR; low direct impact for now.

notable.headline: Labor Department PBM disclosure rule (10-28); CVS ends SilverScript Choice PDP in 13 regions for 2027 (~950k enrollees)
notable.read: Regulatory headwind for Caremark spread economics plus a shrinking Part D footprint. The estimated 10-28 print has not appeared, so the date is unverified.

notable.headline: Apple reportedly tells suppliers to raise iPhone Duo production targets on strong demand
notable.read: Supportive demand evidence set against the hinge-crack replacement program from 10-27. The earnings date (10-29 vs 11-02) remains the key uncertainty; Apple unveiled the touchscreen MacBook Pro on 10-28.

notable.headline: Bitcoin drops to $80,000 after Fed meeting; Cowen warns a hot PCE could trigger a Q4 selloff; Hagerty says the Strategic Bitcoin Reserve could expand after the CLARITY Act
notable.read: Continues the contested-$80k story; price action and rate odds dominate. The legislative item is a mild structural positive but not binding. No exchange failure or adverse regulatory action.

notable.headline: Dropbox cuts about 9% of staff; 8-K 2.02/2.05/5.02 filed 10-28
notable.read: Carried from 10-28: the pre-announced in-line-or-better quarter lowers print risk, but the officer departure under item 5.02 remains unread.
